title: Terms of use
intro: These terms apply when you use Yanig. If you do not agree with them, do not use Yanig.

sections.title: What Yanig is
paragraphs: Yanig is a free website about earthquake safety in the Philippines.
items: It shows recent earthquakes from USGS, GeoNet and BMKG. It checks for new data every 10 minutes.
It gives safety steps for before, during and after an earthquake.
It shows earthquake news from NewsAPI.

sections.title: Yanig is not an alert system
items: Yanig does not send alerts, notifications or warnings.
Yanig cannot predict earthquakes. No one can.
Yanig is not official. For official earthquake reports, go to PHIVOLCS.
In an emergency in the Philippines, call 911.

sections.title: Data can be late or wrong
paragraphs: Earthquake data comes from other agencies. It can be late, missing or wrong.
The first magnitude and place of an earthquake are estimates. The agencies can change them later.
Emergency numbers can change. Check them with your local government.

sections.title: Your part
items: Use Yanig as extra information only.
Follow your local government and emergency officials.

sections.title: Content from others
items: USGS, GeoNet and BMKG own their data. Their own terms apply.
Map data is © OpenStreetMap contributors, under the Open Database License.
News articles belong to their publishers. Yanig shows only the start of each article and links to the full article.

paragraphs: Yanig is given "as is", with no warranty.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: Yanig can stop working at any time. For example, a data source can be down.
Yanig can change or stop without notice.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
paragraphs: These terms can change. The date at the top of this page shows the last change.
If you use Yanig after a change, you accept the new terms.
